case_name: Om Prakash Poddar vs Rina Kumari
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Appellant got married to Respondent on 25.06.2004. After marriage, parties resided at Appellant's native place till 18.07.2004. Thereafter, Respondent started misbehaving with Appellant and his parents.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking divorce to prove desertion.
legal_principles.held: While arriving at the conclusion that the Appellant has been deserted by the Respondent,

legal_principles.principle: A party's failure to file a written statement or contest the case can be considered in determining the credibility of their testimony.
legal_principles.held: She preferred not to file any written statement and contest the case.

outcome.final_order: Decree of judicial separation under Section 10 of Hindu Marriage Act instead of divorce was passed by the trial court. The appeal was allowed, and a decree of divorce was granted.
